chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Stolen uniforms and Ella Fitzgerald taking the Savoy slot
summary: His uniforms are stolen from the car before the Apollo, Alexander pays for new suits, and the Savoy broadcast spot goes to Ella Fitzgerald after Chick Webb's death.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, one reason why is, as I said, before we went in the Apollo, before I went to the theatre, left for New York, I had bought two practically brand new uniforms--I had four or five suits in changes--and we were going down to the theatre the day before to have the uniforms and my suits

pressed, for the opening the next day; the valet got out of the car--I was in the bus and my car-- and goes to see what door he goes in and I think about five minutes or less, when he got back to the car, the car was cleaned out.

Yeah, all my uniforms. So I called up Alexander; he said, my goodness, and to be sure that he wanted everything right as it should be, he called whatever tailor he was doing business with and told him he wanted--I think I had fourteen pieces then--one suit for everyone in the band and two for me. So naturally, that one gig and a date or two I had to pay him; well, Chick Webb had just passed and Ella Fitzgerald was his vocalist, and they decided to make Ella Fitzgerald the bandleader, and Alexander had closed out a deal, we were supposed to go in the Savoy with a nationwide hook-up radio, like Chick had been doing. And so after then, they

decided that we're going to make Ella the band-leader, we're going to have to advertise her as a leader. We just can't say vocalist, so they decided--the corporation owned Ella, owned the Chick Webb band--so they told Alexander and he talked it over and said we'll use Fields some other time, we'll let her run this time and we will put him in right after that, but we have got to build our property.
